column2: I said,
“Probably.”
“But what would they have stolen?{r}{P}”
“Two hundred million yen...
maybe?{r}{P}”
The bank robbery story from before still seemed to be on her mind.
“What about a change of clothes?{r}{P}”
Toshio chimed in.
“Huh?{r}{P}”
“A change of clothes.
Even if he didn't plan to ski, he'd have brought at least a change of clothes.”
“...Normally, sure, but if he was a fugitive, who knows.{r}{p}He may not have had time to pack.”
{n2} was searching the pockets of the hanging coat.
“...There's no wallet or anything either.{r}{p}Did the killer take it?”
“Maybe he wanted to keep the identity hidden.”
Next was the room itself.
We searched around for any personal belongings.
Toshio watched us, shivering.
“Hurry up.”
“If you want out, you can wait outside, you know.”
When I said it nastily, Toshio fell silent.
We looked the room over and even checked under the bed, but found nothing.
That left only the spot by the window, where the body was.
do we really have to examine the body?”
My voice shook from the cold, not from fear.
“Well...
I'll pass.”
I had no choice but to step into the area piled with snow.
With no slippers to speak of, it was like stepping on ice in bare feet.
“Achoo!{r}{P}”
“Achoo?{r}{P}”
“...I just sneezed.”
I slowly went around the bed and carefully peered at where the body lay.
...Fortunately, snow had covered everything and I couldn't see a thing.
My relief was short-lived: I realized that unless I brushed the snow away, it wouldn't count as having examined it.
Damn.
Trembling all over, I brushed the snow away.
There was a rustle, and my hand touched something rough.
...It was frozen hair.
Taking care not to touch the body, I carefully brushed off the snow.
Just like when we first found it, the dismembered body came into view.
Something sour rose from the pit of my stomach.
I don't think Midori came to examine this.{r}{p}It doesn't look like it's been touched.”
“True...
Then what was it?{r}{P}”
{n2} asked from a distance.
“Hey!{r}{P}
Let's go back for now!{r}{P}”
Toshio shouted.
I agreed with that.
Chilled to the bone, even worse than when we'd gone out, we returned to the lounge.
Nobody was missing; everyone seemed safe.
“...Did you find anything?{r}{P}”
Mr. Kobayashi asked, looking at the three of us.
“Nothing.
It seems the killer took everything Mr. Tanaka had.”
With my lips frozen and barely able to speak, {n2} answered for me.
“...I see.
So he really did have a lot of cash or something.{r}{p}Maybe that's what the killer was after...”
Mr. Kobayashi murmured.
“Ugh, I'm freezing.”
I headed for the air conditioner to warm my frozen body.
A rushing sound.
Then a loud noise outside the window.
I flinched for a moment, then remembered it was just snow sliding off the roof.
“Startled again.”
{n2} said, a little amused.
“With a noise that loud, of course anyone would be startled...”
I started to say, then closed my mouth.
“What's wrong?{r}{P}
Hey, you look weird.”
I must have looked really strange, because {n2} asked uneasily.
At that moment, a thought had begun to take shape in my head.
But it was a thought that was hard to accept right away.
I said,
“I know who killed Mr. Tanaka.”
“You really know?{r}{P}{p}Who on earth is it?{r}{P}”
{n2} asked with suspicious eyes.
I didn't answer right away, and began to speak to everyone.
“When the sound of the window breaking came, everyone except Toshio was in the lounge.{r}{p}So at first I thought that if the killer was one of us, Toshio was the most suspicious.”
Everyone looked at Toshio uneasily.
Toshio bristled and shot those looks right back.
“But then I realized that with a trick, even someone who was in the lounge then could have done it.”
When I said that, Toshio's expression eased for a moment.
“A trick?{r}{P}”
{n2} asked.
“A time-lag trick.”
“Time lag?{r}{P}
Like the time-lag attack in volleyball?{r}{P}”
“Right...
We heard the window break and ran upstairs.{r}{p}But we don't actually know if the window really broke at that moment.”
“But...
the window was broken!{r}{P}”
Mr. Kobayashi looked like he couldn't follow.
“That's the time lag I'm talking about.{r}{p}Of course the window was broken.{r}{p}But it didn't necessarily break when we heard the sound, right?{r}{P}”
“The sound?{r}{P}
You just play the sound afterward?{r}{P}”
{n2}'s face suddenly lit up.
“Right.”
I nodded.
“...After dinner, the killer visited Mr. Tanaka's room, killed him, and dismembered the body.{r}{p}Then broke the window without making a sound.”
“How?{r}{P}”

“...For example, there's this method.{r}{p}Cover the whole pane with duct tape and strike it hard.{r}{p}It supposedly muffles the noise and keeps the pieces from scattering.{r}{p}It's a burglar's trick, though.”
“Kid, you know some weird stuff.”
Mr. Kayama stared at me suspiciously, so I hurriedly shook my head.
“I just saw it on TV or something.”
“Okay, I get how he broke the window without a sound.{r}{p}Then what?{r}{P}”
“Then the killer placed a tape recorder he'd prepared somewhere...”
“A tape recorder?{r}{P}
There wasn't one in that room.{r}{P}”
“It doesn't have to be that room.{r}{p}When we first heard the sound, we couldn't tell where it came from, could we?{r}{P}”
“Well, that's true, but...
a tape recorder that could make a sound echo that loudly...
would have to be pretty big, wouldn't it?{r}{P}”
{n2} had hit a sore spot.
“And it seems odd for him to bring a tape of breaking glass recorded in advance...”
Mr. Kobayashi had a point.
“Maybe he recorded it when he actually broke the glass.{r}{p}It would have made a small sound.{r}{p}Maybe he played that back loud...”
“That sound didn't seem like that.{r}{p}Even if you made it louder, I don't think it would sound the same.”
At {n2}'s words, I revised my reasoning a little.
“Then maybe it's this.{r}{p}It really was the sound of breaking glass.{r}{p}But it wasn't that room's window. It was another piece of glass the killer had prepared.”
How about that, I thought, and looked around at everyone.
“But then the killer would still have to break that glass somewhere, right?{r}{P}{p}How?{r}{P}
And how did he bring glass like that in here?{r}{P}”
{n2} piled up one problem after another.
“Those are minor problems.{r}{p}Okay?{r}{P}”
I answered irritably.
“If my reasoning is wrong, then the killer is Toshio after all.
But I can't believe that Toshio, whatever about Mr. Tanaka, would have killed Midori too.”
A faint light flickered in Toshio's dark eyes.
“...Then if it's not me, who the hell is the killer?{r}{P}”
His voice was hoarse.
I was silent a while, organizing my words.

“...Whether it's a tape or something else, if there's a way to make the sound of breaking glass, then people in the lounge could have done it, too.{r}{p}But among them are people who never went to the second floor, or who didn't have the time.
{r}{p}Let's eliminate those people.”
“First, {n2} and I stayed in the dining room until the end after dinner and never went back upstairs.{r}{p}I think there are plenty of people who can confirm that.”

“Next, Mr. Kobayashi was at the front desk after dinner and stayed with us after that.{r}{p}We didn't see Mrs. Kobayashi for a while, but naturally she'd have been in the kitchen cleaning up after dinner.”
When I questioned them with my eyes, the Kobayashis nodded firmly.
“Mr. Mikimoto arrived here a good while after dinner had ended.{r}{p}He was upstairs only briefly, probably just long enough to drop off his luggage.
{r}{p}Even with a chainsaw or something, it would have been impossible for Mr. Mikimoto.”
Since there was no objection, I went on.
“The three office girls...
Kanako, Keiko and Aki went back to their rooms because of that threatening letter, but came right back down to the first floor.{r}{p}They didn't have enough time either.”
Here I fell silent for a while.
I hesitated to go on.
Mr. Kayama asked, his face tight.
I spoke without looking at that face.
“...That's all.
Except for Mr. Kayama and his wife, I've eliminated everyone.{r}{p}Which means one of those two is the killer.”
Haruko stared at me and Mr. Kayama in a daze.
Mr. Kayama spoke, spraying spit.
“What nonsense!{r}{P}
Why would I...{p}I didn't have time to cut up a person either.{r}{p}Same goes for Haruko.
We were together the whole time.{r}{p}Right, Haruko?{r}{P}”
Haruko looked startled, as if caught off guard.
“Wh-
what? Yes.{r}{p}That's right.”
A stomach-churning silence fell.
I broke that silence and went on.

“...Now let's consider the second incident.{r}{p}When Mr. Mikimoto was attacked, the ones outside were Mr. Kobayashi and Toshio.{r}{p}Everyone else, myself included, should have been waiting in the lounge
.{r}{p}With one exception.”
Everyone's eyes focused on Mr. Kayama.
Me?{r}{P}
I was here too, wasn't I?”
“No.
You weren't here the whole time.{r}{p}You went up to the second floor alone to try the cell phone.{r}{p}Saying 'No harm in tryin'.'”

“...Now let's consider the second incident.{r}{p}When Mr. Mikimoto was attacked, the ones outside were of course Mr. Kobayashi, Toshio and me.{r}{p}Everyone else should have been waiting in the lounge
.{r}{p}With one exception.”
Everyone's eyes focused on Mr. Kayama.
“M-me?{r}{P}
I was here too, wasn't I?”
“No.{r}{p}When we came back, Mr. Kayama wasn't there.{r}{p}According to {n2}, he'd gone up to the second floor to try the cell phone.”
was that so...{r}{p}Even if it was, how could I, upstairs, hit Mikimoto, who was outside?”
“If you think about it a little, you'll see it's easy to do.”
I paused and looked around at everyone, but no one said anything.
“Listen.
Mr. Mikimoto was attacked right below Mr. Tanaka's room.{r}{p}And just across the hallway from Mr. Tanaka's room is Mr. Kayama's room.{r}{p}Going back and forth between them without being seen
isn't that hard.”
{n2} gasped.
“Then, then Mr. Kayama attacked Mr. Mikimoto, who was below, from Mr. Tanaka's room...?{r}{P}”
“Probably.{r}{p}It's simple.
Tie a heavy, hard stone or something to the end of a rope.{r}{p}Then wait for the victim to come below, and either drop it or swing it like a pendulum to hit him.”
I gave my arm a light swing to demonstrate.
“That's exactly why Toshio and Mr. Kobayashi, who must have been right nearby, saw no one.{r}{p}After all, the culprit wasn't at the scene.”
I hadn't been confident in this reasoning at first, but saying it aloud, I felt more sure it was right.
“You...
Suddenly, Toshio leaped at Mr. Kayama, who was still seated.
“You bastard!!{r}{P}”
Screaming like a madman, he strangled him.
“Ugh,
gah...
Ngh...”
Mr. Kayama tried to shake off the arms squeezing his neck, but it was hopeless.
At first everyone around just watched, dumbfounded.
But when Mr. Kayama's pained groans reached their ears, Mr. Kobayashi hurried in to stop him.
“Toshio!{r}{P}
Toshio!{r}{P}
Calm down!{r}{P}”
At Mr. Kobayashi's words, Mr. Mikimoto came to his senses too.
“Stop it!
Violence is wrong!{r}{P}”
He rushed to hold Toshio back.
I instinctively shielded {n2}.
“Let go!{r}{P}
Let goooo!{r}{P}”
It took both of them to finally pull off Toshio, who thrashed like a mad dog.
“Gack!{r}{P}
Cough, cough...!{r}{P}”
Mr. Kayama held his throat with one hand and wheezed, coughing.
His wife Haruko was white as paper, only trembling.
“I'll kill you!{r}{P}
I'll kill you for sure!{r}{P}”
Held in a full nelson by Mr. Mikimoto, Toshio still glared at Mr. Kayama with burning eyes.
“Calm down, Toshio!{r}{P}”
Mr. Kobayashi dealt Toshio's cheek a hard
slap.
The loud sound made all of us flinch.
The one who'd been slapped stared blankly at Mr. Kobayashi.
Boss...
why...
why...”
Toshio was so shocked he couldn't speak, and Mr. Kobayashi scolded him with a stern face.
“We can't just declare Mr. Kayama the killer without solid proof.{r}{p}You know that much!{r}{P}”
Then he turned to me.
“{n1}, you too, stop making groundless guesses.{r}{p}You'll only confuse everyone!{r}{P}”
That irked me a little.
But before I could open my mouth, {n2} lashed out at Mr. Kobayashi.
“They're not groundless guesses!{r}{P}{p}Uncle, are you defending him because he helped you out in the past?{r}{P}{p}If you say {n1}'s reasoning is wrong, then rebut it properly.”
Mr. Kobayashi started to speak, but didn't argue back.
Suddenly Aki, the girl with glasses, stood up and shouted.
I don't want to stay with this man! I'm going back to my room!{r}{P}”
“This man,” of course, meant Mr. Kayama.
me too!{r}{P}”
Kanako and Keiko stood up as well.
wait a moment!{r}{P}{p}It's obvious that staying together is safer.{r}{p}So...”
Mr. Kobayashi said in a flustered way, and Aki shot him a startlingly hard look.
“Then tie this old man up somewhere!{r}{P}{p}There's no way we can sit around having tea with a murderer!{r}{P}”
Her shrill shout rang out.
The girl I'd thought of as perfectly ordinary and cheerful was glaring at Mr. Kobayashi with blazing eyes.
It sent a chill down my spine.
“...Anyway, I'm not coming out of my room tonight, no matter what.”
In a tone that brooked no argument, the girls resolutely climbed the stairs.
“A-are you sure?{r}{P}{p}Isn't it dangerous for just the girls...”
Mr. Mikimoto fretted, looking back and forth between their backs and everyone's faces.
“If the killer's dead, everyone can sleep in peace.”
Toshio said, glaring at Mr. Kayama.
“W-what's this,
ya still think I did it?{r}{P}{p}Hey,
Toshio, ya know yer the prime suspect to begin with.{r}{p}Cryin' ain't gonna fool me.”
“What did you say?!{r}{P}
You're still playing dumb?!{r}{P}”
Toshio shouted, red in the face again.
“Please, everyone, stop it already!{r}{P}”
A heartbroken voice rang out.
Kyoko had covered her face with both hands and collapsed in tears.
Toshio stood frozen, looking deflated.
“Suspecting each other like that...
calling each other names...
aren't you ashamed?{r}{P}”
“But...
Ma'am...
he killed Midori...”
Toshio's words didn't reach Kyoko's ears.
It's a lie...
This is a lie...
It's all a dream...
This can't be happening...”
She kept muttering with vacant eyes.
“Kyoko!
Pull yourself together!{r}{P}”
When Mr. Kobayashi called to her and shook her shoulders, she began to cry soundlessly.
Toshio, who'd been watching the two, turned to me and called out.
“Yes?{r}{P}”
“Confident in your reasoning?{r}{P}”
I puffed out my chest.
“Then what do you think we should do?{r}{P}”
Asked that, I quietly studied Mr. Kayama.
He looked a little sulky and looked away.
My reasoning shouldn't be wrong.
But was this man really a killer?{r}{P}
Looking at his actual face, my confidence gradually faded.
Could this good-natured old man commit such a cruel crime?
But if it came to that, there was nobody here who looked like a murderer.
And if amateurs could tell just by looking at a face, the police wouldn't have such a hard time.
“How about this...”
While I was lost in thought, Mr. Mikimoto timidly spoke up.
“I can't say for sure that Mr. Kayama is the killer, but...{r}{p}he's certainly the most likely at the moment.{r}{p}And if, by some chance, he has nothing to do with it, I apologize in advance...
.{r}{p}But considering everyone's safety, don't you think we have no choice but to have Mr. Kayama stay in the cellar or somewhere?{r}{P}”
“The cellar...
I see.”
Toshio glanced at the door beside the entrance.
wait a minute.{r}{p}The cellar, ya say?{r}{P}
Ain't it awful cold down there?{r}{p}I ain't goin' in there, no way.”
As Mr. Kayama shook his head in a panic, Toshio said coldly.
“It's the wine cellar, so it's kept at a proper temperature. It's not that cold.{r}{p}If you're still cold, take a blanket or a hand warmer.”
but...”
I spoke to the still-uneasy Mr. Kayama.
“It's fine, Mr. Kayama.{r}{p}This would protect you, too.{r}{p}If Mr. Kobayashi holds the key, Toshio can't come attack you in the night.{r}{p}And
if you're not the killer, you'd be protected from the real one as well.”
Mr. Kayama thought a while, comparing my face and Toshio's.
“...Yeah, maybe.
Safety-wise, that might be true...”
Finally he nodded, reluctantly.
“All right, it's settled.
That okay with you, Boss?{r}{P}”
Toshio turned to Mr. Kobayashi.
But Mr. Kobayashi was busy dealing with Kyoko, who was still crying, and could only nod.
Toshio went to the front desk, took one of the keys hanging on the wall, and called to Mr. Kayama.
“Right this way, sir.”
I shuddered.
I thought I'd glimpsed an eerie smile on his face for a moment.
“Get me a nice cozy room, now.”
Mr. Kayama said that too, probably as bluster.
“Dear...”
He answered Haruko's worried call with a big nod.
sorry, but could you bring a couple of blankets?”
Opening the cellar door, Toshio turned around.
“...And five or six magazines while you're at it.”
When Mr. Kayama said that, Toshio's face went rigid as he glared at him.
He was probably angry at that shameless attitude.
But in the end he didn't explode.
{n2} went upstairs and came right back down with the blankets and magazines, as asked.
“Well then, g'night.”
Handed what he'd asked for, Mr. Kayama smiled and went through the cellar door.
He slowly descended into the cellar, lit red by a bare bulb.
When Mr. Kayama's back disappeared from view, Toshio slammed the door shut and carefully locked it.
“Now everyone can sleep in peace.{r}{p}Right?{r}{P}”
At Toshio's words, {n2} and I exchanged a glance and nodded hesitantly.
...Right.
There was nothing to worry about anymore
...there shouldn't be.
So what was this unshakable unease?
Back in the lounge, Toshio pressed the key he was holding into Mr. Kobayashi's hand.
“After everyone's up, please let him out.”
“Hm?
Mr. Kobayashi answered in a listless voice.
It was such a feeble reply that you couldn't tell which of them was the employer.
“You two should get some rest, too.{r}{p}There's nothing more we can do.{r}{p}All we can do is hope the weather clears tomorrow.”
“...You're right.{g}
Maybe so...
...Kyoko,
come on, let's go back to our room.”
Kyoko's shoulders were still shaking convulsively as she cried.
Mr. Kobayashi gently put an arm around her shoulders and stood up.
Left behind were {n2} and me, Toshio, Mr. Mikimoto, and Mr. Kayama's wife Haruko.
Is he...
Is my husband really the killer?{r}{P}”
A thin voice reached us.
I was bewildered.
I'd understand her saying “My husband isn't the killer,” but “Is he the killer?” What kind of couple was this?
only reasoned it out from the circumstances...”
“Hey, hey, what's with the lack of confidence?{r}{p}He's the killer, isn't he?{r}{P}”
Toshio said irritably, and I grew even more confused.
“...But is that how a killer behaves...”
Mr. Mikimoto murmured a doubt.
“He thinks there's no evidence, so he's feeling safe.”
Toshio spat out.
“But once the police come, wouldn't forensics turn up plenty of evidence?”
“He must be confident he left none.{r}{p}{p}...Anyway, nobody but him could be the killer.{r}{p}I'm going back to my room.”
With that, Toshio quickly disappeared down the hall.
The rest of us fell silent in front of Haruko.
Head bowed, Haruko opened her mouth.
his second wife.”
Not knowing how to respond, I looked at {n2}, but she seemed just as confused.
“...He's almost too kind to me and the children.{r}{p}But at work they call him a demon boss, an inhuman monster, all sorts of terrible things.{r}{p}He never tells me anything about work,
so I don't know what he's actually done.{r}{p}...I only know one small side of him.”
“...But even if Mr. Kayama did something unscrupulous, that might give someone a reason to resent him, but not to kill him, right?{r}{P}”
I found myself defending Mr. Kayama.
“...But if someone were about to be killed, they might kill in return.”
Mr. Mikimoto said, thinking it over.
That made sense, and I fell silent.
Had that man Tanaka held a grudge against Mr. Kayama and followed him all the way here?
{n2} forced a cheerful voice.
“Anyway, why don't you get some rest too, ma'am?{r}{P}{p}...Thinking any more won't tell us anything.”
She was right.
Haruko seemed to think so too; she gave a feeble smile, stood up and walked off unsteadily.
Haruko climbed the stairs slowly.
Watching her go with concern, Mr. Mikimoto said,
“...Then I think I'll go back too.{r}{p}Wh-what will you two do?{r}{P}”
“Well...”
Of course I'd planned to go back eventually.
But our rooms were separate, which meant being apart from {n2}.
That worried me a little.
Still, I hesitated to suggest spending the night in one of our rooms.
It was unsettling to turn off the lights, so we left everything as it was and went upstairs.
As we climbed the stairs, Mr. Mikimoto suddenly swayed toward me.
“Are you all right?{r}{P}”
“Sorry.
I got a little dizzy...”
But he managed to reach his room on his own feet.
“Well...
be careful.”
With that last remark, Mr. Mikimoto went into his room.
I wasn't sure what I was supposed to be careful about, but it felt like a very fitting thing to say at this moment.
Hearing the click of the lock, I turned to {n2}, standing beside me.
As I started to speak, {n2} cut in.
“...You're not seriously going to leave me alone, are you?”
I was surprised, but also a little relieved.
No!
Of course not.
No way.{r}{p}...Want to come to my room?{r}{P}”
“...Yeah.”
{n2} seemed to relax just a bit and gave a faint smile.
I opened the door to my room and let her in first.
I sat {n2} on one of the beds and took a seat on the other, facing her.
“...Will you stay up with me till morning?{r}{P}”
“Sure.”
My body was exhausted, but I doubted I could fall asleep so easily.
Silence fell.
A night at the inn.
A room with only {n2} and me.
It was something I should have been longing for.
And yet...
I silently reached out and lightly took her hand.
“Midori,
did she really die...”
{n2} murmured.
I couldn't say anything.
“I keep thinking tomorrow it'll turn out it was all an act.{r}{p}Part of the inn's entertainment...{r}{p}and then...
and then Midori would get up all cheerful...{p}Hey,
wouldn't it be nice if that happened?{r}{P}”
Midori was definitely dead.
That was an immovable fact.
But I, too, imagined for a moment the scene {n2} described.
That it was all an act.
How wonderful that would be.
How wonderful...
“I'm
scared.”
“Me too.”
“...Why can people kill
someone?{r}{P}”
{n2} asked a simple question that almost sounded philosophical.
Of course, I had no answer.
“...I can't believe someone like Mr. Kayama killed a person...”
“Me neither.
I'm starting to find it hard to believe too.”
“Really?{r}{P}
So was that reasoning wrong after all?{r}{P}”
I don't think it's wrong yet.{r}{p}But maybe I've overlooked something big...”
If I really was wrong and the killer was someone else, what on earth should I do?{r}{P}
...And if the killer was someone else and there was a new victim?{r}{P}
The thought made me shudder.
{n2} murmured.
“Yes?{r}{P}”
Come closer.”
I silently sat beside her and put an arm around her shoulders.
Her small shoulders trembled in tiny shivers.
No matter what happens, I'll protect {n2}.
I made that embarrassing vow to myself.
Having touched, even a little, and feeling reassured, {n2} and I, worn out in body and mind, seem to have fallen asleep leaning on each other
...Suddenly I woke to find myself sprawled alone on the bed.
Rubbing my puffy eyelids, I looked around the room.
{n2} was gone.
I called out, just in case.
...Still no answer.
Looking at the watch still on my wrist, it was 3:50.
I strained to hear if she was using the shower, but all I heard was the shrill howl of wind through the window.
I stood up and approached the door.
It's open!{r}{P}
Only slightly, but the door was definitely ajar.
I shuddered.
Had someone unlocked the door and come in while I slept soundly...?{r}{P}
And quietly carried off the sleeping {n2}...?
No!{r}{P}
Absolutely not!{r}{P}
There was no way anyone could do that without waking either of us.
Besides, there was no need to.
{n2} had left the room of her own accord, for some reason.
For example, she'd gone back to her room to get something.
Or gone back to her room to use the shower.
Yes...
so as not to wake me, out of consideration...
Either way, she was alone now.
A black unease welled up in my heart.
I had to make sure she was safe.
I had to go get her.
Everyone seemed to be asleep; the hallway was dead silent.
The lights were still on.
Somehow on tiptoe, I made my way to the front of {n2}'s room.
I knocked on the door and called.
No answer.
I pressed my ear to the door and listened for sounds inside.
Again, only the wind.
Even if she were showering, the bathroom was right by the door.
I should have heard something.
I grabbed the knob and turned it.
The door opened so easily it was anticlimactic.
Are you in here?{r}{P}”
Just as I called out,
a scream came from downstairs.
A scream...
A scream when facing true terror can make anyone shudder just by hearing it.
That scream was exactly like that.
{n2} was facing something terrifying and crying for help...
Even knowing that, my legs wouldn't move at all.
I didn't want to see whatever could make her scream like that...
That feeling filled me completely.
Her scream came again.
Weaker than before, colored less by fear than by sorrow.
The second floor was silent, as if everyone had vanished.
I hoped someone would hear the scream and rush out, but there wasn't even a sign of it.
I thought only of getting to {n2} as fast as possible.
Summoning my courage, I headed for the stairs.
...Had these stairs always made this much noise?{r}{P}
